leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members explicitly prefer B041 (topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect) as their round-1 configuration. All six credit Kane and Molenkamp. Five (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) name Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, with citations pairing the Z2 theory with the HgTe experiment; Danielsson instead names Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, with a citation that extends to three-dimensional topological materials. Mehlig and Pearce report moving to B041 after reading the opening ballots (Mehlig from B029, Pearce from B018). Shared reservations are the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, the omission of Fu, Moore and Balents for the 3D story, and possible overlap with the 2016 prize. The supporters do not share a view on the third slot.

Two members explicitly prefer B013 (optical lattice clocks) with the identical pair Katori and Ye and near-identical citations on the invention and development of optical lattice clocks. Both treat it as a single sharp invention with concrete downstream tests (about 1e-18 accuracy, relativistic geodesy, bounds on drifting constants and dark matter, the redefinition of the second). Both list B041 as an alternative, and Kroll states he would not oppose B041 if conceptual reorganisation is judged to outweigh instrumental invention. They share concerns about adjacency to the 2005 and 2012 prizes and about uncredited early lattice work; they differ on conflicts, since Kroll flags a possible one and Lindroth reports none.

areas_of_agreement: B041 and B013 are the only ballots that appear as a preferred configuration in any member's round-1 file, and every member's configuration is a single prize part.
Every B041 supporter credits Kane and Molenkamp and rests the case on a theoretical origin plus a decisive experimental fingerprint in HgTe quantum wells.
B041 supporters regard the field as mature, with fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation across materials and probes, and several call recognition overdue.
Each camp names the other candidate as an alternative (Kroll and Lindroth list B041; Danielsson and Johansson list B013), so B041 and B013 are the two main contenders in this round.
Members who mention B029 say it overlaps heavily with B041 and should not be allowed to split support for one topological story.
scientific_disputes: Whether the 3D topological-insulator discovery by ARPES (Hasan) is part of the core discovery or a separate pillar: Danielsson argues the experimental side deserves two slots, while Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce treat the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp chain from prediction to first observation as the core.
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions already covers the conceptual background of B041; Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig flag this as unresolved.

Whether conceptual reorganisation of a whole field (B041) should outweigh a precisely defined instrumental invention with testable consequences (B013); Kroll and Lindroth frame B013 as an answer to what limits measurement, while B041 supporters stress breadth.
Whether the quantum anomalous Hall realisation (Xue, B029) is a separate achievement or part of the same topological story.
attribution_disputes: Third slot in B041: Mele (joint author of the Kane-Mele Z2 theory; named by Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce) versus Hasan (3D materials by ARPES; named by Danielsson). Danielsson acknowledges that omitting Mele separates a joint theoretical contribution.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum spin Hall state that Molenkamp observed and are outside the credited names; Pearce adds that Zhang's death complicates this question.
Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy, central to the 3D theory, are outside the credited names in every B041 configuration.
For B013, the Katori and Ye pair leaves out Lemonde, Takamoto, Hollberg and the ion-clock groups, and Kroll notes that Ye's contributions are broad, so a Katori and Ye split may look uneven.
Lindroth notes that Ye also appears in a separate ballot, B007, which could affect how the clock credit is framed.
maturity_disputes: B041 supporters describe the field as mature and overdue; the only stated counter is possible overlap with the 2016 prize, not a claim of prematurity.
For B013, Kroll and Lindroth note that the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so part of the case would depend on a future event.

Pearce's own statement raises whether rewarding topological insulators now would leave room for optical lattice clocks in a later year, which is a sequencing question and not a maturity objection to either.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll (B013): research stay in John Hall's laboratory, with Ye's career closely tied to Hall's group, and work in laser stabilisation and precision spectroscopy that feeds lattice clocks; he says this may deserve discussion for possible recusal.

Johansson (B046, not a leading position): work in circuit and waveguide QED, direction of WACQT at Chalmers, and Chalmers links to the 2025 prize; he would consider recusal or caution if B046 were taken up.
Lindroth (B013): field closeness through atomic theory, which she describes as not a personal connection.
Eriksson (B014 and B015, listed as alternatives): subject-matter proximity through magnetism and correlated electrons, not described as a recusal issue.
Pearce (chair): neighbouring astroparticle fields, including B016 (IceCube), would be noted if they came into contention; no recorded tie to any named candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B041, should the third laureate alongside Kane and Molenkamp be Mele or Hasan, and can a citation be worded so that the choice is defensible given that the Z2 theory is a joint Kane-Mele contribution and the 3D materials rest on a separate experimental claim?
How should a B041 citation treat the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang HgTe prediction and the Fu, Moore and Balents 3D theory, which no three-name configuration can name?
Does the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions weaken the case for B041, and if so, what in the quantum spin Hall and Z2 work is new relative to it?
Should B029 be treated as part of the same achievement as B041, and does Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work belong in any citation?
For B013, is the case distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and how much weight should a redefinition of the second that has not happened carry?
If Kroll's possible conflict with Katori and Ye through the Hall group is judged to warrant recusal, how should the committee treat B013 in its deliberation?
If the committee can recognise only one of B041 and B013 in 2026, which criterion should decide: breadth of conceptual reorganisation, or precision of invention and testability?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 is concentrated: six members explicitly prefer B041 and two prefer B013, and no other ballot is the preferred configuration in any of the eight files. Within B041 the attribution is split between five Kane-Mele-Molenkamp configurations and one Kane-Molenkamp-Hasan configuration. The unresolved points are the third slot, the uncredited HgTe and 3D theory authors, the relation to the 2016 prize, and how the committee weighs conceptual breadth against a compact invention in B013.
